summary: SSE reconnect with corporate proxy rewrites strips trailing JSON field leading to partial structured output
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that when an SSE streaming session reconnects behind their corporate HTTP proxy (which performs header rewrites and incremental gzip), the final structured JSON envelope produced by the model is truncated: the last field ("source_metadata") is missing and the JSON array is left unterminated.

Impact:
- Customer workspace shows incomplete JSON responses intermittently (~1-3% of streams).
- Breaks downstream parsers that expect a closing field; customer cannot use streaming in production for their document ingest flow.

Environment:
- Customer: Fintera Bank (enterprise, VPC peering + corporate proxy)
- Region: us-east-1
- API mode: hosted Redwood API via SSE (text/stream)
- SDK: sdk-js v2.3.1 (in-browser behind corporate edge)
- Models observed: redwood/gpt-medium-7b (most common), llama-2-13b in some traces

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Open SSE connection to /v1/streams with Authorization header and client-id.
2) Start prompt that returns structured JSON with a trailing "source_metadata" object and a closing array bracket.
3) Trigger a short network interruption (e.g., disconnect corporate VPN or simulate short proxy restart).
4) Client reconnects and receives streaming segments; final segment is missing the trailing field and closing bracket.

Customer logs and artifacts provided:
- HAR export with partial stream: request ids x-request-id=fin-7a3e (attached)
- tcpdump from customer edge showing HTTP/1.1 chunked frames and a final 0-length chunk missing in some flows (attached)
- SDK trace logs showing reconnect sequence and resume offset (session_resume_offset=18472)

Expected behavior:
- On reconnect/resume the stream should reliably include the full final envelope and termination marker (closing bracket) or a clear end-of-stream sentinel.

Observed behavior:
- Intermittent truncation of the final structured field immediately following an SSE reconnect where an upstream corporate proxy rewrites Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding and injects a keepalive comment line.

investigation_notes:
Summary of findings:
- Reproduced truncated final fragment with nginx proxy that rewrites headers and performs gzip streaming.
- Root cause appears to be a race where upstream edge-proxy rewrites or injects a keepalive comment on the final chunk; when the client reconnects quickly the server runtime treats the final chunk as already consumed and does not re-emit the trailing envelope.
- Evidence: collected server request logs (kibana query: request_id:fin-7a3e) show a successful model generation that includes the trailing field, but the edge-proxy logs show a connection-level rewrite that strips the terminal 0-length chunk / final CRLF in ~80% of failing reproductions.
- Hypothesis: our SSE resume semantics rely on explicit trailing marker bytes; some proxies that rewrite Transfer-Encoding and buffer gzip transform may consolidate or drop that marker during a connection handoff.
- Related internal work: INT-4422 created to patch edge-proxy to maintain explicit end-of-stream sentinel and avoid coalescing last chunk when rewriting headers. Also opened a short-term client-side mitigation in sdk-js (PR linked) to tolerate missing closing bracket by waiting for an end sentinel or validating JSON assembly before emitting to user code.
resolution:
Workaround and long-term fix plan:
- Immediate workaround (applied 2026-03-13): instructed customer to set proxy to bypass gzip and preserve chunked transfer for SSE endpoints. Result: error rate dropped to ~0.1% for Fintera.
- Short-term server-side mitigation (deployed canary 2026-03-13): edge-proxy change to emit an explicit SSE end comment field (":end-of-stream:

") that is independent of chunking framing; servers will also keep a small time window (200ms) to re-emit trailing fragments if a rapid reconnect with matching resume offset is observed. Canary runs in us-east on 10% of traffic.
- Client-side mitigation: sdk-js patched to buffer final reassembly until a sentinel or explicit end event; PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/98. Backported to v2.3.2.
- Long-term: INT-4422 to harden edge-proxy rewrite code to preserve chunk terminators when rewriting headers or injecting keepalives and add a unit test to simulate header rewrite on close. Target rollout to all regions by 2026-03-20 behind a feature flag.

Follow-ups:
- SRE to monitor canary for 72 hours and validate that the sentinel is never dropped (dashboard: Streaming > SSE > end-sentinel-missing).
- Customer success to confirm Fintera production after full rollout.
- Update streaming runbook and SDK migration guide to recommend proxy passthrough settings for SSE endpoints.
